newsitem.title: USA: Arafat almost quit talks Wednesday - Saudi envoy.
newsitem.headline: Arafat almost quit talks Wednesday - Saudi envoy.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat almost abandoned peace talks with Israel early on Wednesday morning, but an item was put on the table that prevented it, Saudi Ambassador Prince Bandar said.
Bandar said he received a call from Arafat early in the morning saying he wanted to leave and go to the airport.
Asked whether a new element was introduced that stopped Arafat from walking out, Bandar replied: "Yes there was, but I can't talk about it."

President Bill Clinton's "positive strong intervention" played a key role in keeping the talks from falling apart at that stage, Bandar told reporters after a speech to the U.S.-Saudi Business Council.
Arafat left Washington on Wednesday evening without making any comment on the summit or its outcome.
"It's been a testing day today for all of us in the Middle East," Bandar said in his speech.
Bandar added later: "Particularly this morning President Clinton should be praised ... he saved the Middle East from blowing up in the last 24 hours."
